r0.why: Definition, gravity, origin under distant weather systems, speed by period/length and little local-wind effect all in [1]-[3].

r1.why: Long wavelength and reason [4], dependence on system/water size [4], >700 m in severe storms [5], sorting and narrower range [8], defined shape [9].

r2.why: Direction coming from, like winds, degrees or compass points with NNW/SW examples in [6]-[7].

r3.why: Origin as wind waves [2], two mechanisms on flat water [21], Phillips 1957 cm-scale waves [24],[33], Miles 1957 shear and exponential growth [26],[27],[35].

r4.why: 'Wavewatch III, which every major weather and climate forecasting centre relies on' - [44] says the sea state models (Wavewatch III only an example) are used by all major centres, not that every centre relies on Wavewatch III.

r5.why: Range of heights [13], significant wave height for reporting [14], highest third over 20 min-12 h [15], trained observer [16], largest less than twice [17].
